title: Relay 5xx
action: The relay is up but the backend is not. NOT AUTOMATED, and the reason is architectural rather than a gap waiting to be closed: the signal is nginx upstream-status lines in the RELAY access log, and the relay is a DIFFERENT HOST. The probe runs beside the backend, which is why the other eleven are countable there - server log lines, /health, the retention report, the reconciliation query - and this one is not. relay_down is covered precisely because liveness is externally observable; a 502 is not, from the backend. Closing it needs the relay to export its access log or report its own 5xx count to a shared endpoint, and both are changes to the relay host rather than to the probe

title: DB disk
condition: any age-based table holding a row past its retention window - ALL SEVEN now, and that word was false for longer than it was true. RetentionLag measured three of six, and the three it missed were the IP-hash tables carrying privacy promises; and usage_daily, one of the original three, could not be MEASURED at all because a DATE column was decoded as an RFC3339 instant, so the read returned an error, the endpoint reported behind=null, and this alert fired on every probe of every real database. auth_attempts is the seventh, added with its 7-day sweep: it is the credential-guessing counter behind the five _per_hour caps, and it was absent from this report while its per-address half held a salted hash. Both earlier faults are fixed; the row is kept explicit because the claim it now makes was false in three different ways
source: docs/observability.md (the "DB disk" row of the Alerts table)

title: Error rate >5%
condition: PROCESS-LIFETIME, not a 5 min window - the counters are cumulative fetch_adds since process start, so a brief spike on a long-running service cannot lift the ratio and this alert UNDER-fires. A real 5-minute window needs a ring buffer the counter does not have
threshold: 5% of all responses served since the process started
